correctness.rationale: Let m=n-r+1 and rows M_{r−1}, columns M_r. For each row s the interlacing binary matrix R admits column t(s)=(s_1,...,s_{r−1},m−1); lexicographic ordering makes the selected square minor unit triangular, proving a Z-right inverse. For weighted deletion, represent each multiset by a monomial; E is D=sum_i partial/partial x_i on homogeneous degree r. The integer unimodular substitution y_0=x_0, y_i=x_i−x_0 turns D into partial/partial y_0 in every degree. Thus its integral diagonal coefficients are j with multiplicity binom(n−j−1,r−j), j=1..r when r<n. This proves the stated cokernel cyclic summands (not necessarily ordered Smith factors) and the characteristic-p rank formula sum_{p∤j}binom(n−j−1,r−j), full iff p>r. At r=n, E=[n],R=[1], including the degenerate single-symbol boundary. Independent direct multiset enumeration, modular ranks and Smith comparisons verified all 21 n,r pairs 1<=r<=n<=6, but only the integral argument proves the universal classification.
